messages.subject: Construct variables
parts:
Hi All,

I am doing cfa analysis using lavaan. But I have very fundamental question that most of you may already know the answer. 
Firstly:
I have 12 to15 variables which are binary, discrete and continuous (such as net income, wealth and age). Can I use them at the same time? or should standardize the continuous variable (or define ordinary variable for each class of income?).

Second: 
My data is collected from 8 countries and I want to control for that. Should I make 7 binary variables out of them and include them as controls?

I attach my model here:

Thank you very much for your help!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Construct variables
parts:
lavaan can estimate models with any combination of binary, ordered, and continuous outcomes.  It is bad practice to "standardize" variables prior to analysis; you can simply request a standardizedSolution().  

Your other questions are more general than about the lavaan software, so I would recommend looking for general guidance on SEMNET:

https://listserv.ua.edu/cgi-bin/wa?SUBED1=semnet&A=1

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
